issue.title: Name-reservation staleness proof rebuilds a 35MB registry under the global name lock, convoying every launch
issue.description:
Found while investigating why `sase bead work ws -Y` on apollo (2026-09-05, ~14:11-15:01 local) ran 50+ minutes with ~39 minutes of pure user CPU while launching only 3 of the epic's phase agents.

## Root cause

Every name-reservation read pays the full registry staleness proof and rebuilds on any mismatch:

- `_load_registry_for_reservations` (src/sase/agent/names/_registry.py) resets scan caches and calls `load_name_registry(trust_stale_proof_memo=False)`.
- `registry_file_is_stale` (src/sase/agent/names/_registry_store.py) compares a `source_signature` whose `count` includes **every artifact directory on the machine** (apollo: 20,441). Any agent launch anywhere creates a new artifacts dir, so the registry is stale again almost immediately.
- `rebuild_name_registry()` then rescans all artifact dirs + dismissed bundles and rewrites the registry JSON (`json.dump(indent=2, sort_keys=True)`) **while holding the global `~/.sase/agent_name_allocation.lock` flock**.

On apollo the registry is 35.7MB with 11,962 entries (`source_signature.count` 20,441). ~6,300 entries are historical imports from machine athena (`athena.sase*` 4,952, `athena.toobig*` 798, ...), i.e. v1 agents-sync import output — the leg epic sase-ws is removing. One rebuild burned ~5.5 min CPU (runner PID 1342300: 5m30s CPU over 11m24s elapsed while holding the lock, machine at load ~11/16).

## Observed convoy

/proc/locks on apollo showed the flock on agent_name_allocation.lock (inode 575127) held by an agent runner child at 100% CPU with three waiters queued behind it: the `sase bead work` parent, a second runner, and a `sase monitor start` process. When the runner finished (registry rewritten 15:01:34), the monitor process took the lock next and bead work queued again. `wchan=locks_lock_inode_wait` on the bead-work parent confirms it blocks there.

Effect on `sase bead work`: bead_work launch-timing entries for the same epic earlier the same day show total 1537.9s (outcome=error; agent_launch 931s, prompt_render 508s) and 3479.7s (outcome=ok; agent_launch 2000s, force_reuse_cleanup 1163s). Spawns in the current run were 16 min apart with continuous user CPU between them and near-zero syscall time — consistent with repeated rebuild/proof work, not I/O.

Secondary symptom: phase runners hit `Ignoring stale SASE_AGENT_PLANNED_NAME='sase-ws.3' because its registry reservation does not belong to artifacts directory ...` and fall back to generic `ace(run)-<ts>` names, so epic phases lose their deterministic `sase-ws.N` identity.

## Remediation directions (needs planning)

- Make the reservation-path staleness proof incremental (per-directory tree signatures already exist in `_registry_scan.py`) instead of a whole-machine artifact-dir census per reservation.
- Bound or GC the registry: 12k entries dominated by dead cross-machine v1 imports; epic sase-ws (import-leg removal) bears directly on whether those entries can be pruned.
- Shrink the critical section: don't hold `agent_name_allocation.lock` for the full rescan+35MB rewrite; rebuild outside the lock and swap in, or shard the lock.

Related: sase-cl fixed the same scan class on the *display/publication* path (scanfix, sase-ej.1); the reservation path intentionally still pays the full proof. sase-ww (propose-to-gate 8m09s stall, same host, same morning, "dominant cost unexplained") plausibly shares this cause.

task_type_fields.impact: Every agent launch on the machine serializes behind multi-minute registry rebuilds: sase bead work runs take 26-58+ min per attempt, monitors and runners queue on the same flock, and phase agents lose deterministic sase-<epic>.N names via the stale-reservation fallback.
task_type_fields.repro: On a host with a large registry (apollo: ~/.sase/agent_name_registry.json 35.7MB, 11,962 entries, source_signature count 20,441), run 'sase bead work <epic-id>' while other agents launch. Watch /proc/locks for agent_name_allocation.lock (holder at 100% CPU, waiters queued) and wchan=locks_lock_inode_wait on the bead-work PID; agent_launch_spawn timing entries land 15+ min apart.

payload.description: sase-cl fixed the same unbounded registry staleness scan on the display/publication path (scanfix); sase-wy is the reservation path, which intentionally still pays the full proof and rebuilds under the global name lock
same host and morning: sase-ww's unexplained 8m09s propose-to-gate stall plausibly sits behind the same agent_name_allocation.lock rebuild convoy documented here
roughly half the bloated registry entries are v1 agents-sync imports from athena; epic sase-ws removes that import leg and bears on whether those entries can be GC'd
